clue.text: Southern elite? That's a laugh

parts.note: the cream is the best part, the elite of any group

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a southern elite, dismissing it as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a' links the wordplay to the definition: calling something 'a laugh' or 'a scream' means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something hilarious is called a laugh or a scream, the two nouns being synonyms.

clue.text: Agreement in case

definitions.meaning: a pact or contract between parties
a small case holding face powder and a mirror

explanation.surface: An agreement is placed inside a case.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a formal pact; the other is a small powder case carried in a handbag.

clue.text: Rock up half-heartedly for a joint

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
half-heartedly removes one of the two central letters, half the heart

parts.note: to rock is to wobble

explanation.surface: Something rocks upwards without much enthusiasm for a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one B from the double-B heart, giving WOBLE, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm's hinge between upper arm and forearm is a joint.

clue.text: Important event and men lose it, getting drunk

indicators.note: getting drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: At a big occasion the men lose control by getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant stage or landmark in development is figuratively an important event.

clue.text: Lots in America complain when drinking raki, oddly

parts.note: to carp is to complain or nag

indicators.note: drinking means one piece swallows another, so the letters go inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word raki

explanation.surface: An American grumbles while downing the anise spirit raki.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the first and third letters of 'raki', which 'drinking' tucks into the word for 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans speak of parking lots, so 'lots' in the US is the British word for places to leave vehicles.

clue.text: Girl from school losing good name

indicators.note: losing means the letter is dropped

parts.note: a college is a school

explanation.surface: A girl from a school is said to have lost her good name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Irish word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Wild attack capturing the north of Bosnia

indicators.note: capturing means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: in a down clue the north of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A savage attack seizes northern Bosnia.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious or fanatical, as a rabid supporter, means wild.

clue.text: Stone from blast area all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Stone from an explosion site is scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine white translucent mineral used for carving is a kind of stone.

clue.text: Eager to finish early, accepting Blair perhaps brought up the central theme

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other piece inside
to finish early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tony Blair, former UK prime minister, gives the first name

explanation.surface: An eager politician, maybe Tony Blair, raises the main theme of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish early' cuts KEEN to KEE, and 'brought up' turns TONY into YNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal idea of a speech or conference is its central theme.

clue.text: Sign on telephone lines — 'This moves volumes'

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a mobile is a cell telephone
Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A notice taped to a phone line announces something that shifts large quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volumes' looks like quantities but means books; a travelling van of books is what literally moves them.
explanation.definitionFit: A van-based lending service carries books, or volumes, from place to place, so it literally moves them.

clue.text: Sack women on non-professional new seat

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: lay means not belonging to a profession, as a lay person

indicators.note: new signals the word seat is made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Women are dismissed in favour of an amateur being given a new seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ASTE from 'seat'. 'Sack' is the verb to plunder, not to fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder and devastate it, which is to ravage it.

clue.text: Somebody intimidating academic must adopt kid

indicators.note: must adopt means the academic takes the other piece in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
to kid is to tease, as is to rag

explanation.surface: A lecturer is told to take in a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, formidable person, often a woman, is figuratively called a dragon.

clue.text: Almost unable to shift firm plaster

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the phrase's synonym is dropped

parts.note: stuck means fixed and unable to move
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm plaster is nearly impossible to move.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine plaster used for coating walls and for mouldings.

clue.text: Boxes must contain fruit for horses

indicators.note: must contain means the boxes hold the other piece

parts.note: chests are boxes
a nut is a fruit

explanation.surface: Boxes are to hold fruit fed to horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddish-brown horses are called by this colour name, so they are horses.

clue.text: Details of one European bitten by strange insect

indicators.note: bitten by means held inside the jaws of the other piece
strange signals that the word insect is rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A European suffers a bite from an odd bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges INSECT to NICETS, and 'bitten by' puts IE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine points or small precise matters of etiquette are subtle details.

clue.text: Party on a river tower

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party
the Nile is an African river

explanation.surface: A party is held on a riverside tower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Italian bell tower, usually freestanding beside a church.

clue.text: Climbers may be fawning types around Her Majesty

indicators.note: around means the fawning types surround the other piece

parts.note: creeps are sycophants who fawn on others
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Social climbers are imagined as sycophants hovering near the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests social climbers but means plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants such as ivy that grow up walls and supports are climbing plants.

clue.text: Display of colours by gunners in front

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Soldiers parade their colours with the gunners at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colours' suggests regimental flags but means the spectrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectrum colours seen in the sky after rain is a natural display.

clue.text: Ring assistants for more food

definitions.meaning: a boxer's helpers in the ring corner
a further helping of a meal

explanation.surface: Helpers at a boxing ring go back for more food.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's corner aides go by this name; it also means further helpings at a meal.

clue.text: Rumour of spirit being rejected twice

indicators.note: twice means the reversed piece appears two times
being rejected means the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads about a drink turned away two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A low whispered report or hint of gossip is a rumour.

clue.text: Not knowing of a conflict within a Parisienne

indicators.note: within means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a, as a Parisian woman would say
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman is oblivious to a war going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant of something or oblivious means not knowing about it.

clue.text: Restaurant brother needs to cover first

indicators.note: needs to cover means the brother goes round the other piece

parts.note: 1st, written IST with I for one, means first

explanation.surface: A sibling has to pay for the first restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal eating place is a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Speak in terror at educational

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone speaks in fear at a school event.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a formal or pompous speech is to speak.

clue.text: Rubbish cold drink some sent back

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

indicators.note: sent back means the word is reversed

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: A cold drink is returned, partly because it was rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious nonsense or empty talk is rubbish.

clue.text: Works land, even sending son south

indicators.note: sending means the letter is moved from its place
in a down clue south means to the bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: still can mean even, as in 'still better'

explanation.surface: A farmer works the land, even sending a son down south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending son south' moves the S of STILL from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate or plough the ground is to work the land.

clue.text: Plant producing a Bolivian glue

indicators.note: producing signals that the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A plant yields a South American adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tropical climbing shrub with bright papery bracts, native to South America.

clue.text: Writes off about street con artists

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
off means the letters of writes are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a pair of swindlers as finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles the six letters of 'Writes' to TWIERS; 'about' wraps that round the street abbreviation. 'Writes off' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers or cheats are informally called this, from twisting the truth.

clue.text: Consumer welcoming small festival

indicators.note: welcoming means taking the other piece in

parts.note: an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A shopper is welcomed at a modest festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' suggests a shopper but means someone who eats.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Christian spring feast of the resurrection, a church festival.
